name: Empty Islands
summary: A mouse click replaces the invalid diagonal in the earlier replay. It collects all four chips and completes at tick 920 in native Tile World MS and TWO with identical traces. It fails in SuCC because mouse target timing and force-floor input rules differ; Microsoft CHIP.EXE compatibility is unverified.
proofSteps: Keep the Empty-over-Water bridge at (1,8),(2,8) unused. Wait until a Teeth covers the upper teleport (0,7), then enter the lower teleport southward. Because MS skips covered teleport destinations, Chip emerges onto the outer force-floor circuit. The replay uses random seed 67 and starts this maneuver at tick 85.

Collect the right-island chip (23,16), return through the original right-island entrance, then collect the center chip (19,17) and lower-left chip (17,16). Hidden chips require leaving and reentering after the covering Empty tile disappears.

Return to the left force lane with a gap behind another creature. At tick 742, left-click visible tile (0,10). Chip begins this tick at (0,12); forced movement puts him at (0,11), and the mouse goal adds a north step to (0,10). The original mouse handler emits absolute command 832, which the live engine records as relative mouse command 177. This reaches the brief window where the upper teleport is covered, so teleportation fails and Chip advances onto starting Gravel (0,8) at tick 746.
Cross the preserved bridge, collect the final hidden chip (14,8), then open socket (17,8), leave and reenter for the flippers beneath it. Swim to exit (31,0).

The corrected TWS contains only original MS cardinal keyboard commands and one mouse command. It completes the unchanged DAT in both engines at tick 920 with all four chips collected. The full native and TypeScript traces match.

experiments.result: Exact DAT metadata/layers decoded; initial production runtime loaded and rendered with repository sprites.

experiments.inputs: 140 idle ticks, N for 1 tick, then idle
experiments.result: Chip reaches (0,4) at tick 148 while both Empty-over-Water bridge cells remain intact. This invalidates a simple no-return argument for the initial island.
Initial bridge intact; Chip at (1,23); returning west collides with a jammed creature.

The earlier 146-byte replay used N+E command 9 at tick 743. Original MS keyboard input cannot emit that command; passing replay verification did not make it a legal player solution. It is replaced by a normal mouse click at tick 742, with no replay-mode override during construction.

experiments.kind: original live mouse input and recorder
experiments.result: The unchanged native input module maps a left click on visible tile (0,10) to command 832, followed by three Preserve polls. A temporary CLI parser submits those live commands to unchanged native gameplay code: completion at tick 920, with the native recorder emitting relative mouse command 177 at tick 742. All 161 recorded moves match the exported replay; 921 gameplay snapshots match native replay.

Unmodified SuperCC commit 3e92380dabbae2dcf4e86ed5dc7572695311c8d4 fails this exact 147-byte replay. Its replay loader resolves relative mouse command 177 before the forced move, targeting (0,11); Tile World resolves it after that move, targeting (0,10). A second probe supplying the intended absolute target (0,10) still fails: SuCC explicitly suppresses a mouse move in the current slide direction, while Tile World tests the raw command before mouse conversion. Both SuCC probes end with Chip dead at (1,6), after half-tick 374. See 376-supercc-audit.json and its source links and reproduction files.

A blocked Teeth at (0,24) causes a remote Walker at (29,16) to miss a forced move at tick752. All764 steps match native Tile World exactly, but this delays the wrong creature: the upper teleport is not held for Chip and the lower teleport subsequently jams. Bounded launch-time, route, seed and stepping variations have not produced a keyboard-only return. These negative experiments are not an impossibility proof.

limitations: This is a verified original Tile World MS solution, with a matching TWO replay. It is not a verified Microsoft CHIP.EXE solution. The earlier diagonal replay is withdrawn as a player-valid solution.

SuCC rejects the required extra mouse step even when supplied the intended absolute target. Changing only the replay's relative mouse coordinates is therefore insufficient. The comparison establishes an engine difference; it does not establish which implementation matches Microsoft CHIP.EXE. A cardinal-keyboard-only solution remains under investigation.

legacy_c/mslogic.c:1396-1434 (only uncovered teleport destinations are considered)
legacy_c/generic/in.c:338 (left click emits absolute map command)
legacy_c/generic/in.c:419 (MS keyboard returns one cardinal command)
legacy_c/mslogic.c:1373 (mouse goal is processed after force-direction filtering)
legacy_c/mslogic.c:1386 (mouse goal movement occurs on tick phase 2)
